title: Casimir force screening by a quantum Boltzmann plasma
authors: Petr Brandyshev, Maksim Koniushenko, Yury Budkov
abstract: We develop a finite-temperature field-theoretical description of the Casimir interaction between two perfectly conducting boundaries with the intervening gap filled by a two-component quantum Boltzmann plasma embedded in a homogeneous dielectric background. The quantum motion of the charged particles is represented by imaginary-time worldlines, while the electromagnetic field is treated in the Gaussian approximation. The resulting partition function contains distinct longitudinal and transverse response contributions and an additional quantum-induced source term with no classical counterpart. In the classical limit the theory reduces to the usual Casimir-screening picture: the static longitudinal mode is Debye screened, whereas the transverse electromagnetic sector is unaffected by classical mobile charges. Finite thermal de Broglie wavelengths modify the nonzero Matsubara response and produce the leading quantum correction to the force. In the static long-wavelength limit, the longitudinal dielectric function has, through the leading quantum correction, the same expansion structure as the Lindhard response of a degenerate electron gas under the correspondence $k_{TF}\leftrightarrowκ_D$ and $k_F\leftrightarrowλ_{dB}^{-1}$, while the static transverse response reproduces the leading high-temperature Landau orbital diamagnetic susceptibility.
summary: This work provides a detailed field-theoretical framework to calculate the Casimir force screening exerted by a quantum Boltzmann plasma between conducting plates. It successfully separates classical and quantum contributions, demonstrating that quantum effects manifest as a measurable correction to the force, particularly through the modification of the longitudinal dielectric response.
main_problem: The paper develops a finite-temperature field-theoretical description to calculate the Casimir interaction force between two perfectly conducting boundaries when the intervening gap is filled by a two-component quantum Boltzmann plasma.
main_result: The theory quantifies the quantum correction to the Casimir force, showing that finite thermal de Broglie wavelengths modify the Matsubara response and that the longitudinal response structure matches the Lindhard dielectric function under formal correspondences.
method: The calculation employs field theory, treating the electromagnetic field in the Gaussian approximation and representing particle quantum motion via imaginary-time worldlines. The free energy is derived from the partition function, separating longitudinal and transverse response contributions.
model_or_system: The system is a two-component Coulomb plasma (positive and negative charges) confined between parallel, perfectly conducting plates separated by distance L, embedded in a dielectric background. The plasma is modeled using quantum Boltzmann statistics.
key_observables: Casimir free energy, longitudinal and transverse response functions, and the quantum-induced source term.
important_parameters: Temperature (T), number density (n), plate separation (L), and the coupling parameter $\Gamma$. Key regimes include the classical limit and the crossover between classical and quantum plasma behavior.
main_assumptions: The theory relies on the Gaussian approximation for the electromagnetic field and treats particles as structureless point charges, neglecting exchange and full quantum degeneracy effects in the leading order.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the force gradient comparison between classical and quantum predictions for a $	ext{Li}^+$-electron plasma in liquid ammonia, showing the separation and the magnitude of the quantum correction.
paper_structure: The paper builds the theory by deriving the effective action using worldline path integrals, decomposing the resulting free energy into longitudinal, transverse, and source terms. It analyzes the classical limit, derives the quantum corrections from finite Matsubara modes, and explicitly calculates the source contribution ($\ln Z_4$).
why_interesting: While focused on plasma physics, the rigorous application of finite-temperature field theory to boundary effects and the explicit calculation of quantum corrections to macroscopic forces are highly relevant to open quantum systems and quantum electrodynamics in structured media.
